newsitem.title: USA: Greyhound to buy Carolina Trailways for $20.3mln.
newsitem.headline: Greyhound to buy Carolina Trailways for $20.3mln.

text.p: Greyhound Lines Inc said Monday it has signed a definitive agreement to buy Carolina Trailways Inc of Raleigh, N.C., for $20.3 million of cash and Greyhound common stock.
The transaction is subject to approval of the U.S. Surface Transportation Board.
Carolina will become a wholly owned subsidiary of Greyhound Lines, and will be operated separately by its existing management.

Carolina Trailways, said the company, had gross revenues of about $16 million last year and Greyhound expects this transaction will improve its earnings per share. In addition, the company has identified significant operating efficiencies which will make the transaction even more accretive to earnings. The deal also includes some excess real estate and other assets that will be sold, said the company.
The company said the purchase of Carolina is the first step to complement internal growth with growth through acquisitions.
Carolina Trailways operates intercity bus service to 21 cities in North Carolina and Virginia, and from Norfolk north to Washington, Baltimore and Philadelphia.
